newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - CBOT gains shut off demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - CBOT gains shut off demand.

text.p: Limit-up gains in CBOT soymeal futures shut-off demand from end-users Friday, brokers said.
"This rally has pretty much killed all the pricing interest that was out there," said one river dealer. "There's not even any interest in the beans."
CBOT May soymeal futures were up the $10.00 per ton trading limit in early trade. At 1037 CST, May was up $8.50 at $274.50 per ton.
Some brokers also expressed surprise at the continued heavy pace of the weekly crush.
The National Oilseed Processors Association on Thursday put the weekly crushing pace at 30.106 million bushels, above trade expectations for 29.24 to 29.90 million bushels.
"I certainly couldn't detect any downtime in this direction," said one Indiana-based merchandiser. "I imagine we'll keep burning this crush margin as long as there are beans around."
Conditions on the Ohio River have improved dramatically in the areas where flooding had shut off access to transportation, dealers there said.
